question: The kinetic energy of the constitute molecules of the matter is minimum for its:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Solid state**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• he **kinetic energy** of the constituent molecules of matter is related to their motion. 
 
• The **kinetic energy of the constituent molecules** of matter is minimum for its solid state. 
 
• In a solid, **the molecules are tightly packed together **and can only vibrate in place,
 
• It results in the **lowest kinetic energy **compared to liquids and gases where molecules have more freedom of movement. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Liquid State (Moderate Kinetic Energy)**

 
 
• In liquids, molecules are **loosely arranged** and have weaker intermolecular forces compared to solids.
 
• They can move around each other, giving liquids **a definite volume but no fixed shape**.
 
• Since molecules have more freedom of movement than in solids, **kinetic energy is higher than in solids but lower than in gases**.
 
 
 
• **Gaseous State (Maximum Kinetic Energy)**
 
 
• In gases, molecules are **widely spread out** with very weak intermolecular forces.
 
• They move randomly at high speeds in all directions.
 
• Since gas molecules are in constant motion with high velocity, **they possess the maximum kinetic energy**.
